failures.title: Peugeot DW10C Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: DPF & EGR Clogging - Urban Driving Issues
items.whatHappens: Like all modern diesels, the DW10C's Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) and Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) system are prone to clogging, particularly on vehicles used primarily for short urban journeys where the DPF cannot complete a regeneration cycle. Symptoms include reduced power, increased fuel consumption, and warning lights. This is the most common maintenance issue on the DW10C.
items.repairVsReplace: DPF cleaning is a specialist job (£200-£600). EGR valve cleaning or replacement is also manageable (£200-£500). These are repairable issues and rarely require engine replacement. Read our full DPF failure guide

items.title: Injector Failure - Misfires & Poor Running
items.whatHappens: The DW10C uses piezoelectric injectors that can fail, causing misfires, rough running, poor starting, and increased fuel consumption. This is particularly common on high-mileage examples or those with poor fuel quality.
items.repairVsReplace: Injector replacement is a specialist job (£200-£500 per injector). Replacement of all four injectors is often recommended if one has failed, as the others are likely to follow. This does not typically require engine replacement. Read our full injector failure guide

items.title: Swirl Flap Failure - Intake Manifold Issues
items.whatHappens: The DW10C's intake manifold has swirl flaps that can become stuck or break due to carbon buildup. This can cause performance issues, rough running, and in severe cases, the broken flaps can be ingested into the engine, causing catastrophic failure.
items.repairVsReplace: Swirl flap repair or intake manifold replacement is a specialist job (£300-£800). If flaps have broken and been ingested, the engine is typically beyond economical repair - a full replacement is the only option. Read our full intake manifold failure guide

items.title: Timing Chain & Turbocharger Wear - High-Mileage Issues
items.whatHappens: The DW10C uses a timing chain that can stretch over time, particularly on high-mileage examples or those with extended oil change intervals. The turbocharger can also suffer from wear, particularly if oil changes have been neglected.
items.repairVsReplace: Timing chain replacement is a specialist job (£800-£1,500). Turbocharger replacement is also manageable (£600-£1,500). Neither typically requires engine replacement.

failures.goodYearsLine: The DW10C was introduced in 2010 as an updated version of the DW10 HDi with improved emissions control. Post-2015 engines benefit from improved DPF regeneration strategies and software updates that reduce the frequency of regeneration issues. However, the DPF and EGR issues are inherent to all modern diesels with urban use - regular motorway driving to allow DPF regeneration is essential. Using the correct oil (PSA B71 2312) and fuel additives can help extend component life.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the DW10C
variants.intro: The DW10C is the 2.0-litre BlueHDi diesel engine, available in multiple power outputs across the Stellantis range. It's part of the DW10 family, which also includes the earlier HDi variants and later updated BlueHDi versions. The DW10C is distinguished by its common rail injection system, variable geometry turbocharger, and emissions control systems. Where the code appears: - Stamped on a metal plate on the engine block (left-hand side, near the timing cover) - On the V5C logbook under "Engine number" (the first 6 characters will read DW10C) - Via VIN decoder - the BlueHDi family is identified by the model designation Commonly confused with: - [DW10 - LINK PENDING - page not in current inventory] - the earlier 2.0 HDi (110-163 hp), predecessor to the DW10C, different injector and emissions system - DV5RC - the 1.5 BlueHDi, smaller capacity and lower torque; not interchangeable - [DW10D - LINK PENDING - page not in current inventory] - updated BlueHDi variant with improved emissions and software; not a straight swap without ECU changes - [DW10F - LINK PENDING - page not in current inventory] - the 2.0 BlueHDi with 180 hp, higher performance variant with larger turbocharger and injectors

Used different injector technology and emissions systems - the DW10C introduced improved common rail and BlueHDi emissions control.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement DW10C - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used DW10C can be viable for lower-value Peugeot 3008 or Citroën C5 models where the car's value doesn't justify a recon unit. However, the DPF, injectors and turbo are the biggest risks - only consider a used unit with documented proof of recent DPF cleaning, injector service, and turbo inspection. Without that, factor in £800-£1,500 for preventative work (DPF cleaning, injectors, timing chain inspection). Link once: /services/used-engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A proper DW10C recon is the best option for owners planning to keep their car long-term, especially for the heavier 3008, 5008 and C5 where the engine works harder. A quality recon should include: full strip and inspection, new injectors (critical), DPF cleaning or replacement, EGR valve service, new timing chain and guides, turbocharger inspection/refurbishment, new gaskets and seals, and a full test. With a 12-24 month warranty, this gives you peace of mind that the engine's known weaknesses have been addressed - well worth the £1,200-£2,200 supply cost. Link once: /services/reconditioned-engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full rebuild is justified when the original engine has suffered catastrophic failure (swirl flap ingestion with valve damage, severe injector failure causing cylinder wash, timing chain failure) and the car is a cherished keeper or low-mileage example. An upgraded rebuild should include new pistons/rings, refreshed cylinder head, new timing chain and guides, and a full DPF/turbo overhaul. This is specialist territory and typically only makes sense for cars with strong residual value. Link once: /services/rebuilt-engines

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** All engines can be supplied and fitted through our network of vetted Peugeot diesel specialists nationwide, with 12-month warranty on reconditioned and rebuilt units. Link once: /services/supply-and-fit
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: ** The DW10C sits in Peugeot 3008, 5008, 508, Citroën C5, C4 and DS models - cars now worth £3,000-£15,000 depending on age and condition. With a reconditioned supply cost of £1,200-£2,200, replacement is viable on most examples. However, for a sub-£2,500 3008 or C5 with high mileage and a failed engine, a used unit (£400-£900) with documented history may be the only sensible option. For cars worth under £2,000, consider breaking the car before committing to a replacement engine. For the heavier 5008 and C5 where the DW10C is the default diesel, a reconditioned unit is strongly recommended to ensure longevity and reliability.

items.question: What are the most common failures on the DW10C BlueHDi engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are DPF and EGR clogging (particularly with urban driving), injector failure (piezoelectric injectors failing on high-mileage examples), swirl flap failure in the intake manifold, and timing chain wear on higher-mileage examples. The DPF and EGR are the most common maintenance items on the DW10C. DPF/EGR: regular motorway driving (20+ minutes) for DPF regeneration is essential. Injectors: preventative replacement recommended at 80k-100k miles. Swirl flaps: intake manifold inspection at 60k-80k miles.
bullets: DPF/EGR: regular motorway driving (20+ minutes) for DPF regeneration is essential.
Injectors: preventative replacement recommended at 80k‑100k miles.
Swirl flaps: intake manifold inspection at 60k‑80k miles.

items.question: Which models use the DW10C 2.0 BlueHDi engine?
items.answer: The DW10C was fitted to Peugeot 3008 (I & II), 5008 (I & II), 508 (I), 308 (I), Citroën C4 (II), C5 (X7), C4 Picasso (I & II), C4 Cactus, DS 4 and DS 5 between 2010 and 2018. Available in 130 hp, 150 hp and 180 hp variants. Not to be confused with the older DW10 HDi or the newer DW10D/F. Not to be confused with the 1.5 DV5RC (which replaced the DW10C in many models).

items.answer: A used DW10C can be viable for lower-value Peugeot 3008 or Citroën C5 models, but only if it has documented proof of recent DPF cleaning, injector service, and turbo inspection. Without that, factor in £800-£1,500 for preventative work (DPF cleaning, injectors, timing chain inspection). A reconditioned engine is the safer choice - it includes new injectors, DPF cleaning, new timing chain and gaskets, with a 12-24 month warranty. Used is cheaper (£400-£900) but DPF, injector and turbo risks are significant. Reconditioned addresses all known weak points and gives peace of mind.

items.question: How do I confirm if my car has the DW10C or the DW10D/F?
items.answer: Check the engine code stamped on the block (left-hand side near the timing cover) - it will read DW10C for the 130-150 hp variant, or DW10D/F for later updated variants. The V5C logbook also lists the full engine number, with the first 6 characters identifying the code. DW10C: 130-150 hp, used 2010-2018. DW10D: 130-150 hp, updated emissions and software (2018+). DW10F: 180 hp, larger turbo and injectors.
bullets: DW10D: 130-150 hp, updated emissions and software (2018+).
DW10F: 180 hp, larger turbo and injectors.

items.question: How long does a DW10C engine typically last?
items.answer: With meticulous maintenance and early preventative work, these engines can exceed 150,000-200,000 miles. The DW10C is a robust engine; the limiting factors are the DPF, injectors and swirl flaps. DPF/EGR: regular motorway driving for regeneration is essential. Injectors: preventative replacement recommended at 80k-100k miles. Timing chain: preventative inspection at 80k-100k miles.
